First, we rewrite the integral as

$$
\int (5x-1)^{-6}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=5x-1.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5x-1)^{-6}\,\text{d}x & =\int {u}^{-6}\cdot \frac{1}{5}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\int {u}^{-6}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-\frac{1}{5}){u}^{-5}+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{25{u}^{5}}+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{25(5x-1)^{5}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[-\frac{1}{25(5x-1)^{5}}+C] & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[-\frac{1}{25(5x-1)^{5}}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =-\frac{1}{25}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[(5x-1)^{-5}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =-\frac{1}{25}\cdot (-5)\cdot (5x-1)^{-6}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x-1)+0 \\  & =\frac{1}{5(5x-1)^{6}}\cdot 5 \\  & =\frac{1}{(5x-1)^{6}}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
